what_this_file_is: The repository's declaration of which Zenodo DOI belongs to which release. One row per
deposit, appended at release time and never rewritten: a version DOI is frozen to the
bytes of one deposit forever, so a row that is here is a permanent fact.
platform/check_version_stamps.py enforces it. OFFLINE it holds every live citation
surface to the DOI declared for the current VERSION, and -- because the superseded rows
are kept -- it can answer 'that DOI belongs to v1.0.0' about a surface that names an old
one, which is the sentence that makes the defect obvious. With --remote it resolves the
concept DOI through the Zenodo API and confirms this file against what Zenodo says the
latest version is.
WHY THIS IS A FILE OF ITS OWN and not a field in CITATION.cff, codemeta.json or
biotools.json: each of those IS a live citation surface. A declaration that lived inside
one of them could only ever prove that surface agreed with itself, and the defect this
closes is a surface that confidently agreed with itself while naming the wrong deposit.
The declaration has to be somewhere no reader is ever sent to cite from. It is the same
arrangement retractions.jsonl has with platform/check_retractions.py: a hand-maintained
root-level ledger that no surface reads, and a guard that holds the surfaces to it.
AT A RELEASE: the webhook mints the version DOI only after the tag is pushed, so nothing
can fill this in ahead of time. Append the new row here first, then write the same DOI
onto CITATION.cff and biotools.json and rebuild data/dataset.json. Run the guard; it
names every surface that still points at the previous deposit.
concept_note: Minted once, for the record as a whole. It always resolves to the newest PUBLISHED
version and is the DOI a reader normally cites. It is never superseded and never
appears in the versions list below.

versions.note: Superseded by v1.1.0 and still a correct name for one thing: the bytes of the 2026-08-20 deposit, whose description counts the slate at eight. That record was never corrected in place -- see docs/REGISTRATION.md §1 -- so it will always say eight. Kept here because the guard's whole message depends on it: a surface that names this DOI is told which version it belongs to, and that is what makes the error legible.
